To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the number of responses emitted during extinction is a function of the instructions provided before extinction and the schedule of reinforcement during conditioning.
subjects' responding during extinction following FR conditioning was a function of the instructions given them prior to extinction.
the number of extinction responses made during extinction following FR conditioning is controlled by the pre-extinction instructions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role that instructions play in the control of human operants during extinction.
the effect of instructions upon the rate of human operant responses during extinction following a fixed-ratio schedule of reinforcement.
the effects of instructional control on the rate of extinction responding following fixed-ratio reinforcement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the subjects were not responding in extinction because of the instructions.

the subjects who received no maximum-reinforcment instructions during extinction made more responses than those who received instructions that the maximum number of reinforcement were obtainable during FR conditioning, and that those who received instructions correctly indicating the number of maximum reinforcements obtainable made fewer responses than the other groups.
the instructions given prior to the extinction phase of an experiment may have an influence on the amount of extinction responding that is exhibited by the subject.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
instructions can be used to control human operant behavior during extinction.
subjects who are given instructions which indicate that reinforcement is available will respond at higher rates than subjects who are not given such instructions.

the effects of instructions on extinction responding are a function of the subject's perception of the instructions and the subject's perception is influenced by the subject's previous conditioning experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that
instructions can be used to control responding during extinction, but the instructions must accurately reflect the contingencies in place during conditioning.
instructions can be used to influence the behavior of humans.
instructions can control responding during extinction following FR conditioning.
